title: Velmarite
text: Velmarite is a layered silicate catalogued during the second regional survey. Specimens are pale green with a waxy lustre. The hardness of velmarite is 4.5 on the scratch scale. It cleaves along two planes.

title: Thornodite
text: Thornodite occurs as dark prismatic crystals. It is recovered from cooled vent deposits along the eastern ridges. Field notes record a faint metallic odour when a crystal is freshly broken.

title: Cindralite
text: Cindralite forms thin crusts on exposed basalt. The colour of cindralite ranges from rust to deep brown. The hardness of cindralite is 3 on the scratch scale.

title: Obrekite
text: Obrekite has a measured density of 3.1 grams per cubic centimetre. The only recorded locality is the southern scarp, where it fills narrow fractures.

title: Yalvanite
text: The colour of yalvanite is deep blue and it occurs in coarse grains. The hardness of yalvanite is 6 on the scratch scale. It is found across the western flats.

title: Durnexite
text: Durnexite crystallises late in cooling flows and sits in open cavities. Cleavage is poor and uneven.

title: Pellomite
text: Pellomite is straw yellow with a resinous lustre. The density of pellomite is 2.6 grams per cubic centimetre. The hardness of pellomite is 2.5 on the scratch scale.

title: Sarnakite
text: Sarnakite is found as blocky masses in the northern terraces. Individual masses reach half a metre across.

title: Quelbrite
text: Quelbrite shows a bright submetallic lustre on fresh surfaces. The hardness of quelbrite is 5.5 on the scratch scale.

title: Mirovanite
text: The colour of mirovanite is grey with a faint violet cast. It grows in slow cooling pockets well below the surface.

title: Taskelite
text: The hardness of taskelite is 7 on the scratch scale. The density of taskelite is 3.4 grams per cubic centimetre. Cleavage is perfect in one direction.

title: Grendalite
text: Grendalite is olive green and gives off a sharp odour when wetted. It occurs along the inner canyon walls.

title: Catalogue entries
text: Specimens entering the archive are catalogued by survey season and given a six character label. The catalogue records the collector, the locality and the date of entry.

title: The scratch scale
text: The archive measures hardness on a ten step scratch scale. A specimen is assigned the step of the softest material that scratches it.

title: Sample storage
text: Samples are stored in sealed trays at a steady temperature. Trays are kept away from direct light because several pale crystals fade.

title: Survey seasons
text: The regional survey ran in four seasons. Each season covered one sector of the island and ended with a sorting week.

title: Label format
text: Labels use three letters for the sector and three digits for the order of entry. A label is never reused after a specimen leaves the archive.

title: Cleavage descriptions
text: Cleavage is described as perfect, good, poor or absent. The description refers to the quality of the break and not to its direction.

title: Lustre descriptions
text: Lustre is recorded as metallic, submetallic, waxy, resinous or dull. Readings are taken on a fresh surface under diffuse light.

title: Density readings
text: Density is measured by water displacement and reported in grams per cubic centimetre. Readings are repeated three times and averaged.
